To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extracellular c AMP phosphodiester-ase-inhibitor and membrane differentiation systems are independent of each other and are regulated by exogenous c AMP.
the extracellular cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) phosphodiesterase system and the membrane differentiation of Dictyostelum discoideum amoebae are regulated independently by extracellular cAMP.

exogenous cAMP stimulates ePD activity and represses PDI synthesis in D. discoideum, and that these effects are not dependent on the activation of the adenosine 3′,5′-cyclic monophosphate (cAMP) adenylyl cylase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the cAMP phosphodiysterase inhibitor system in Dictyostelioium discoideum.
the regulation of the extracytoplasmic cAMP phosphodi-esterase-inhibi-tor system in the development of the cellular slime mold Dictyostelium.
the regulation of the ePDI system by exogenous c-AMP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exogenous cAMP stimulates the ePD-PDIsystem and membrane differentiation independently, but the stimulation of membrane differentiation requires a high concentration of cAMP.

the extracellular cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) phosphodiesterase system and membrane differentiation in Dictyostelidum discoideum are independent of each other, and are both regulated by the same exogenous cAMP pulse.
the ePD system and membrane differentiation in D. discoideum are regulated independently by cAMP and that the cAMP pool is regulated by cAMP only in a limited set of circumstances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

exogenous cyclic AMP regulates the extracellular cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase activity and the synthesis of its inhibitor by a mechanism that is independent of the adeny cyclase and that this regulation is independent of membrane differentiation.
the cAMP pulse regulates the ePD-PD system by an extracellular mechanism, whereas membrane differentiation and the intracellular cGMP pool are controlled by an intracellular mechanism.
the ePD and the PDI are controlled independently of membrane differentiation by exogenously added cAMP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cAMP pulses are not only a signal for aggregation but also a signal for differentiation.

cAMP can regulate membrane differentiation and the cAMP pool independently of the ePD and PDI system, while the ePDI system is regulated by cAMP independently of the cAMP receptor, adenylyl cylcase, and cAMP pool.

the cAMP phosphodiasterase-inhibitor (ePD-PDI) system and membrane differentiation can be regulated independently by extracellular cAMP and that the regulation of the ePDI-PDI system does require activation of the cAMP receptor.
